links.comparator_used: Non-reasoning variant of the same model (Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen3-32B, Gemini-2.5-Flash), standard mode
links.outcome: Rate of correct responses on BiasMedQA bias-inducing vignettes
links.tradeoff: Reasoning did not reliably reduce bias susceptibility; Gemini-2.5-Flash accuracy fell to 47.4-86.1% on four unpublished bias prompts, suggesting possible training-data contamination and brittleness.
links.quote: In all three models, the reasoning-enhanced variant achieved higher rates of correct responses (Llama-3.3-70B: 72.5-82.1% vs 61.0-73.4%, Qwen3-32B: 71.7-78.7% vs 55.5-64.1%, Gemini-2.5-Flash: 81.8-88.6% vs 80.0-83.7%).

links.effect: Statistically significant reductions in biased responses across all three model architectures (no numeric effect sizes given in the abstract)
links.quote: The debiasing and few-shot prompting approaches demonstrated statistically significant reductions in biased responses across all three model architectures.
